Files, search, editing and terminal all live on the remote box."},{"id":"p6s1","text":"**Zero install on the server.** No vscode-server-style remote agent, no daemon, nothing to download "},{"id":"p6s2","text":"— a standard OpenSSH server is all it takes."},{"id":"p7s1","text":"> 中文文档：README.zh-CN.md"},{"id":"p8s1","text":"## Why"},{"id":"p9s1","text":"DSH's agent runs on your local machine. When your code, data or production box lives on a remote Lin"},{"id":"p9s2","text":"ux server, you either SSH in separately or fight with sync tools. Competing remote solutions ship a "},{"id":"p9s3","text":"fat remote component (hundreds of MB) that must be downloaded to the server on first connect."},{"id":"p10s1","text":"`dsh-cloud-workspaces` takes a different route: everything rides **standard SSH channels** (exec / S"},{"id":"p10s2","text":"FTP / PTY via ssh2). The server needs nothing beyond what it already has."},{"id":"p11s1","text":"## Features"},{"id":"p12s1","text":"### Cloud workspaces (the headline)"},{"id":"p13s1","text":"- **Dual-pane workspace picker** — a source rail (this machine / recent workspaces / SSH hosts) besi"},{"id":"p13s2","text":"de a directory pane with breadcrumbs, an editable path, empty/error states and inline folder creatio"},{"id":"p13s3","text":"n; cloud workspaces are adopted by DSH's official workspace registry and show up in every session pi"},{"id":"p13s4","text":"cker as `host / path`.
- **Transparent toolset redirect** — when a session's cwd falls under a cloud"},{"id":"p13s5","text":" placeholder, the plugin registers same-named `bash` / `read` / `write` / `edit` / `glob` / `grep` /"},{"id":"p13s6","text":" `read_image` tools **into that session's own agent scope**, so the agent keeps calling the tools it"},{"id":"p13s7","text":" already knows while every call executes on the server. Local sessions are untouched — the shadowing"},{"id":"p13s8","text":" is per session, and falls back to the official local tools the moment a session isn't a cloud one.
"},{"id":"p13s9","text":"- **Shadow tools with official UI** — session-scoped remote `bash` / `read` / `write` / `edit` / `gl"},{"id":"p13s10","text":"ob` / `grep` register in the agent's scope only, and implement the official `presentCall` / `present"},{"id":"p13s11","text":"Result` presenters, so chat rows render as real terminal / read / search cards — expandable, copyabl"},{"id":"p13s12","text":"e, native.
- **Background jobs** — `run_in_background: true` on `bash` / `ssh_exec` starts the comma"},{"id":"p13s13","text":"nd as a first-class DSH job (`job_output` / `job_list` / `job_kill`, completion notices, jobs UI): i"},{"id":"p13s14","text":"nstalls, builds and test suites run on the server without ever hitting an exec timeout.
- **Port for"},{"id":"p13s15","text":"warding** — `ssh_tunnel start` maps `127.0.0.1:<port>` through the connection to a host reachable fr"},{"id":"p13s16","text":"om the server (remote web previews, loopback-only databases, internal hosts). `stop` / `list` manage"},{"id":"p13s17","text":" live forwards; they close when the connection drops."},{"id":"p14s1","text":"### SSH settings card (in DSH Settings → SSH Connections)"},{"id":"p15s1","text":"- **Host manager** — display name, host, port, user; **password auth** (keyboard-interactive aware —"},{"id":"p15s2","text":" works with PAM/Ubuntu servers that never offer the plain `password` method) or **private key** (pat"},{"id":"p15s3","text":"h to a key file).
- **Connection test** — one-click probe with latency; saved credentials are reatta"},{"id":"p15s4","text":"ched server-side (the browser only ever sees a redacted view).
- **Remote directory browser** — list"},{"id":"p15s5","text":", navigate, **create** and **delete** folders on the server; then **bind any directory as a cloud wo"},{"id":"p15s6","text":"rkspace** in one click.
- **ProxyJump** — jump-host chains, per-hop credentials."},{"id":"p16s1","text":"### Security"},{"id":"p17s1","text":"- Host configuration lives in a private per-user file under `~/.dsh/` with owner-only permissions (0"},{"id":"p17s2","text":"600, plus a restrictive ACL on Windows). **Passwords are never written to DSH's settings store** — t"},{"id":"p17s3","text":"hey go only to that file. A legacy `dsh-remote-ide-hosts` section left in `settings.yaml` by earlier"},{"id":"p17s4","text":" versions is **read once and left untouched**: plugin 0.4.x does not rewrite or delete it, so remove"},{"id":"p17s5","text":" that section manually after confirming the hosts appear in the settings card (see `docs/upgrade-to-"},{"id":"p17s6","text":"0.2.md`). The settings card sees a redacted view and can never read a stored credential back.
- Remo"},{"id":"p17s7","text":"te sessions are scoped: shadow tools exist only inside sessions bound to a cloud workspace. Local wo"},{"id":"p17s8","text":"rkspaces are never affected.
- **Server host keys use trust-on-first-use (TOFU).** The first success"},{"id":"p17s9","text":"ful handshake records the server's `SHA256:` fingerprint in the private host file; later connections"},{"id":"p17s10","text":" to that host must present the same key. A changed key **fails the handshake by default** with an er"},{"id":"p17s11","text":"ror that warns about a possible man-in-the-middle attack and names the recorded and presented finger"},{"id":"p17s12","text":"prints; after confirming the server really was re-keyed, delete and re-add the host or remove its `h"},{"id":"p17s13","text":"ostKey` field from `~/.dsh/dsh-remote-ide.json` to trust the new key. Changing a host's hostname or "},{"id":"p17s14","text":"port drops the old fingerprint (a different endpoint). Pooled connections are verified once per conn"},{"id":"p17s15","text":"ection, as OpenSSH does. The record is local to this plugin and is **not** shared with `~/.ssh/known"},{"id":"p17s16","text":"_hosts`.
- Remote file reads are capped at 2 MiB: a larger file is read as a stream of its first 2 M"},{"id":"p17s17","text":"iB and returned with `truncated: true`, never buffered whole in the host process.
